conviction_note: Two measurements that disagree only in size. The findings sum to +0.7: company-guide arithmetic says the revenue range is likely to be raised again, and the name paid +11% and +19.1% for its last two revenue beats. Against that sits a September oil and freight re-escalation that threatens an EBITDA guide already pinned at the low end. abs_move 12 rests on the 15.0% option-implied move (indicative only, 50% ATM spread, 400 contracts of open interest) and the last confirmed earnings reactions (+19.1, +11, +3.7). p_up is 56 because the positive is guide arithmetic, not an unseen number, and the stock is falling into the print (-7.4% over 5 days).
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $241M (3 analysts, range $241-242M), from one aggregator snippet only (https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/OTLY/analysts, page behind a login, not verified). Cross-check against the company guide: the FY26 guide is +8-10% constant-currency growth with a 200-250bp FX tailwind (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001843586/000184358626000021/otly-ex99_1.htm). Taken against FY25 revenue of $862.5M (197.5+208.4+222.8+233.8) and H1 FY26 actual of $468.4M, that guide implies a Q3 of roughly $235-245M. The $241M sits in the upper half of the guide-implied range. EBITDA bar: FY guide $25-35M 'toward the low end', and H1 delivered $5.4M (Q1 $5.0M + Q2 $0.4M), so H2 needs about $19.6M against $14.1M in H2 2025. No Q3 EBITDA or EPS consensus could be sourced. The revenue bar has a single unverified source, so the reported-quarter sizes are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 397,081 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 1.27% of 31.23M shares outstanding, 5.77 days to cover, down from 697,565 on 2026-07-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/otly/short-interest?range=6m, FINRA via aggregator). Not a crowded short, though days to cover are moderate because turnover is thin (about 70k shares/day, roughly $0.8M). Skew is null in the baseline. Put/call OI is 1.12 on only 400 contracts and the ATM spread is 50% of mid, so the options say almost nothing about direction. Sell-side: Barclays cut its target to $13 from $14 on 2026-10-16 and kept Overweight; consensus target $14.39 across 5 analysts (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/OTLY/forecast/). Spot $11.84 is -7.4% over 5 days, +4.1% over 20 days and -25.5% from the 52-week high.

findings.finding: Revenue momentum is running well above what the raised FY guide implies for H2. Q2 constant-currency growth was +12.7% and H1 about +10.5%. The +8-10% FY guide implies only about +5.8-9.6% in H2, on a Q3 2025 comparison of +3.8% cc. The North America large-foodservice-customer headwind 'has substantially ended' (Q2 call). A second guide raise and a Q3 above the $241M bar (a Q2-pace cc growth rate gives about $249M) are more likely than not.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The name pays for this line. Q2 2026 (2026-07-22): revenue $240.1M against $220.05M consensus plus the cc guide raised from 3-5% to 8-10%; the stock rose +19.1% (baseline). Q4 2025 (2026-02-11): revenue $233.8M against about $216M; the stock rose about +11% (https://finviz.com/news/309616/otly-stock-gains-11-despite-reporting-wider-than-expected-loss). Q1 2026: revenue +15.6%, guide only reiterated; the stock rose +3.7% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The bar has caught up with the Q2 level ($241M against $240.1M actual), but the guide still implies H2 cc deceleration that Q2's segment volumes (Europe +16.9%) and the end of the NA headwind do not show. If the market had priced a second raise, the stock would not be -7.4% over five days and 25% off its high into the print with only a $13-14 sell-side target band. The name has beaten the revenue consensus by 8-9% on two of the last three prints, which suggests a thinly covered (3-analyst) bar that keeps anchoring on the guide.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript, CFO and Global President on H2 phasing and the NA customer headwind ending: https://www.webull.ca/news-detail/15273923783435264 (2026-07-23). Company's March 2026 capacity release cites European plant-based drink demand +6% and Oatly foodservice +20%+: https://www.itiger.com/news/2617411055 (2026-03-05). Both are company sources, so they are not fully independent of the 6-K.

findings.finding: The FY26 adjusted EBITDA guide ($25-35M, 'toward the low end') was explicitly conditioned on the Middle East conflict impact not worsening, with Q3/Q4 cost impact expected 'broadly in line with Q2'. In September the conflict re-escalated: Dated Brent rallied to $114.26 on 2026-09-09 (above $100 for the first time since late July) with record tanker freight, and oil freight is reported up sevenfold on 2026-10-22. That raises the risk that the low end is cut or framed as at risk. H1 delivered only $5.4M of the $25M low end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025: rose about +11% despite an EPS miss, because revenue led. Q1 2026: the guide was reiterated with Middle East cost caveats and the stock rose +3.7%. The EBITDA line has not yet been the swing factor on a print, so its reaction function is unknown.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is -7.4% over five days and Barclays trimmed its target on 2026-10-16. But no sell-side or company source ties the September escalation to Oatly's EBITDA guide. If it were priced, a target cut citing costs or an EBITDA estimate below $25M would be visible. Q2 Brent peaked at $126 (April 30), so the Q3 average may not exceed Q2's, which is why this is sized as a risk and not a call.
findings.independence: Freight surge reported 2026-10-22: https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2026/10/22/war-triggers-sevenfold-surge-in-oil-freight-rates. The company's own conditioning language is in the Q2 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001843586/000184358626000021/otly-ex99_1.htm). This is a macro-to-company proxy that the company has not confirmed.

findings.finding: Barclays (Overweight) cut its OTLY price target to $13 from $14 on 2026-10-16, a preview trim 12 days before the print. Its stated reason could not be sourced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not determinable. Earlier Barclays target moves (cut to $12 from $14 around Q2, then raised to $14) bracket a +19% print.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. It is public, and the stock fell below its 50-day average on 2026-10-21 and is -7.4% over five days. Filed so the panel sees the sell-side's pre-print direction.
findings.independence: Tickeron reports the same $14 to $13 cut 'mid-October': https://tickeron.com/ticker/OTLY/. It is the same event, not independent.

findings.finding: Balance sheet at 2026-06-30: $344.4M of interest-bearing debt classified as current (including about $336M of 9.25% PIK convertibles due 2028) against $44.6M cash, negative equity of $23.5M, and FY26 free cash flow guided negative. No new financing or going-concern language was found. Nordic bonds were listed on Nasdaq Stockholm around 2026-09-28, and revolver covenants were reset in the 2025 refinancing until Q3 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on a print. The 2025 refinancing was not a print-day event.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The convertible notes were already current at 2025-12-31. Asked what the money buys: inventory and capex for volume growth (CFO), with no covenant pressure visible. So it is near zero, filed only because a convertible-refinancing update or cash burn could surface in the Q3 release.
findings.independence: 2025 refinancing terms: https://www.panabee.com/news/oatly-refinances-130-million-debt-secures-covenant-relief-with-sek-750-million-credit-fa. Different source, same overhang.

findings.finding: Raw oat costs eased. Swedish farmgate oat prices were about $0.16/kg in July 2026, down 26.6% year on year (FAOSTAT-based series), and German feed oats were flat at €0.205/kg into October. That is a possible small gross-margin support beside the energy and freight headwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin expanded +1.9pp in Q1 and +1.4pp in Q2. The reactions were driven by revenue and guidance, not margin.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody covering a 3-analyst name models oat inputs. Oatly contracts oats ahead, so the transmission to Q3 is uncertain and the size is tiny.
findings.independence: Oat futures and EU cash prices: https://commodity-board.com/oats-pause-after-september-surge-as-futures-firm-cash-stays-flat. This is a weak, low-quality proxy.

outside_window.finding: Greater China strategic review (Q2 segment adj. EBITDA -$1.5M, plus $0.8M of review costs in the quarter) is due to complete 'prior to the end of the year'. Bloomberg reported in June 2026 that local management is weighing a buyout. A decision could come with Q3 but is dated to year-end, and exiting a loss-making segment would be a mild positive.

Q3 2026 EPS or adjusted EBITDA consensus (no source found)
Circana/Nielsen/Kantar oat-milk scanner data for 2026 in Europe or the US (none public)
Danone Q3 2026 sales as a peer read (Danone reports 2026-10-28, the same day, so not before the print)

Notes to the H1 interim report (the EDGAR page served only the primary statements, so I could not confirm why the convertibles are classified current)

rejected_candidates.candidate: Finanztrends article claiming Q3 2026 revenue of $208M (+10.9%)
rejected_candidates.detail: The figures match Q3 2024; Q3 2026 has not been released, and the 2026-09-28 company notice dates the release to 2026-10-28. This is a mislabelled old story.

rejected_candidates.candidate: The baseline's 8-event reaction history as an earnings base rate (median 3.96%)
rejected_candidates.detail: The baseline itself flags a 17-day cadence as implausible: it includes the 2026-09-24 bond prospectus and other non-earnings 6-Ks. I used only confirmed prints instead (Q4 2025 +11%, Q1 2026 +3.7%, Q2 2026 +19.1%).

rejected_candidates.candidate: Landskrona plant capacity expansion of $16M, from 150 to 200M litres, by March 2027
rejected_candidates.detail: Dated 2026-03-05 and long known. It is used as independence for the momentum finding rather than as its own finding.

baseline_tension: The positive momentum finding cuts against the -7.4% five-day slide and the Barclays preview trim, but agrees with the name's demonstrated habit of rallying on revenue beats. There is no usable skew to contradict either sign.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar from one unverified source): revenue momentum and guide raise cut +3.5 to +3.0. The guide-arithmetic half stands on the company's own 6-K; the beat half rests on a single-source $241M.
Rule 6 (resolves after the window): Greater China review (+1.0) moved to outside_window because the company dates completion 'prior to end of year'.
Rule 5 (macro-to-company proxy not confirmed by the company): Middle East/oil EBITDA risk cut -2.5 to -2.0.
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): Barclays target trim cut -0.5 to -0.3 so it carries only the sourced trim, not the five-day slide.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): convertible/current-debt overhang cut -0.3 to -0.2 after asking what the money buys (inventory and capex for volume growth, no covenant pressure).
Rule 8 and the guidance-change row: abs_move_pct raised from 11 to 12 on a thin, 3-analyst name likely to move its guide; p_up unchanged at 56.
